description:
Host is one physical machine as the operator found it through its BMC. The operator creates it and names it after the machine's serial number, in lower case; the label metal.pk.io/asset names the Asset it was found by. You read it to see the state of the machine: kubectl get hosts shows the asset, serial, vendor and phase, and kubectl describe host <name> shows why it waits.

A HostClaim binds a Host for use. To take a machine out of the operator's hands for hardware work, set the metal.pk.io/maintenance annotation on it.

fields.name: spec
fields.description: HostSpec is written by the operator from the HostClaim that binds the machine; you do not edit it. Everything else about a Host is what the operator found, not what anyone wrote.

fields.name: claimRef
fields.description: ClaimRef names the HostClaim that holds this machine. The first claim to set it wins; any other claim on the same machine waits (HostAlreadyClaimed). The UID pins the exact claim: a claim deleted and created again under the same name is a new claim.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the object.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: The namespace of the object.

fields.name: uid
fields.description: The UID of the object. An object made again with the same name has a different UID.

fields.name: os
fields.description: OS is the TalosNode this machine should run, copied from the claim and cleared when the claim is released. Until it is set, a bound machine is reserved and nothing is done to it.

fields.name: nodeRef
fields.description: NodeRef names the TalosNode (os.pk.io) whose config this machine boots.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the object.

fields.name: status
fields.description: HostStatus is what the operator found out about the machine itself.

fields.name: blockedOn
fields.description: BlockedOn says why the host is not moving on (Approval(Provisioning), SerialMismatch, HostInMaintenance); a reason, not a phase, because it can happen in any phase.

fields.name: conditions
fields.description: Conditions are the truth — the only thing reconcilers branch on.

fields.name: lastTransitionTime
fields.description: The time of the last change of the status.

fields.name: message
fields.description: A message for people about the last change. It can be empty.

fields.name: observedGeneration
fields.description: The generation of the object that the condition is for. A lower value than metadata.generation shows an old condition.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: A word in CamelCase that tells why the condition has its status.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The status of the condition: True, False or Unknown.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The type of the condition.

fields.name: firmwareProposed
fields.description: FirmwareProposed remembers the last firmware plan proposed for this machine, so the same plan is not proposed twice. Written by the firmware lane only.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: Operation is the proposed HostOperation as namespace/name.

fields.name: planHash
fields.description: PlanHash is the sha256 of the desired state the operation serves.

fields.name: identity
fields.description: HostIdentity identifies the machine, whichever BMC it is reached through: the same machine seen through two BMCs gets the same identity, and so one Host. Vendors put the serial number in different places (Huawei on the system, Supermicro on the board); the operator reads the right one for each.

fields.name: serial
fields.description: Serial is the machine's serial number: the board serial on Supermicro, the system serial on Huawei and other vendors.

fields.name: lastResetTime
fields.description: LastResetTime is when the BMC last saw the machine reset. When it moves and no operation explains it, the Drifted condition says somebody reset the machine another way (ipmitool, the BMC web page, the power button). Not every BMC reports it (Huawei iBMC does not); drift is then not detected.

fields.name: managedBy
fields.description: ManagedBy lists the ways to reach the machine — usually one BMC.

fields.name: endpointRef
fields.description: EndpointRef names the ManagementEndpoint (the BMC).

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the object.

fields.name: reachable
fields.description: Reachable says whether this BMC answers.

fields.name: systemId
fields.description: SystemID is the Redfish ComputerSystem id behind that BMC.

fields.name: phase
fields.description: Phase summarizes the conditions below for people and for kubectl columns. It is a summary, not the contract: automation should read conditions.

fields.name: systemFirmwareProposed
fields.description: SystemFirmwareProposed is the system-firmware lane's plan memory, the same guard as firmwareProposed for the components a reset applies.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: Operation is the proposed HostOperation as namespace/name.

fields.name: planHash
fields.description: PlanHash is the sha256 of the desired state the operation serves.
